tasks.title: Rename RotateDirection.cs to RotationDirection.cs, content byte-identical
acceptance: src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/RotationDirection.cs exists and src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/RotateDirection.cs does not. Verified by `ls` on both absolute paths. This encodes dotnet-format.md:57, section 2 File Organization: "File name matches the type name exactly: `RegisterUserCommand.cs`". The type is already named RotationDirection (measurement.md section 2, read at RotateDirection.cs:3), so the file name is the only thing wrong.

The new file's content is byte-identical to RotateDirection.cs at 00a093a: exactly three lines, every one CRLF-terminated, the third reading `public enum RotationDirection { Clockwise, CounterClockwise }`. Verified by `cat -A` on the new path showing exactly three `^M$`-terminated lines and no `$`-only terminator. This is load-bearing and not cosmetic: git detects a rename by content similarity at diff time, so any content change in the same commit as the move drops the similarity of this ~95-byte file below the rename threshold and the move is recorded as a delete plus an add. T2 adds the documentation to this file afterwards, as a separate task, for exactly that reason.

`sed -i` was not used on this file, and no command rewrote its line endings. The repository-wide ban is recorded in measurement.md section 4: `sed -i` rewrites whole-file CRLF to LF and fails the build. Evidence: the `cat -A` output from the criterion above, plus the task naming the mechanism it used to move the file.

Preservation criterion, deliberately satisfied at startRef: neither src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/ControlsPaletteView.xaml.cs nor src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs is modified, and `grep -o 'RotationDirection' <file> | wc -l` still returns 3 and 2 respectively. Those two files reference the type and not the file, so a file rename must leave them untouched; the per-file counts 3 and 2 were derived by the architect with that command at 00a093a and sum, with this file's 1, to the 6 occurrences measurement.md section 2 reports.

tasks.title: Add XML documentation to the six undocumented Floors types
acceptance: Each of the six types ObjectKind, ObjectRotation, ObjectScale, SnapAnchor, RotationDirection and ScaleDirection carries a `<summary>` on its own type declaration. Verified by reading the declaration line of each of the six files. This encodes dotnet-format.md:372, section 9: "All public types, members, and parameters must have XML documentation comments." Baseline from measurement.md section 3: five of the six files contain zero `<summary>` tags and ObjectKind contains exactly one, which documents its None member at ObjectKind.cs:5 and not the type declaration at ObjectKind.cs:3.
Every member of SnapAnchor carries its own `<summary>`. The population is the 5 members at SnapAnchor.cs:5-9 (Center, North, South, East, West), read from the file.
Every member of ObjectRotation carries its own `<summary>`. The population is the 4 members at ObjectRotation.cs:5-8 (None, CW90, CW180, CW270), read from the file.

Every member of RotationDirection carries its own `<summary>`. The population is the 2 members Clockwise and CounterClockwise. They sit in a single-line enum body, so satisfying this requires expanding that body to a braced multi-line form; that structural expansion is expected and in scope.

Every member of ScaleDirection carries its own `<summary>`. The population is the 2 members Up and Down at ScaleDirection.cs:3. They too sit in a single-line enum body that must be expanded to a braced multi-line form.
Each of the four public constants on ObjectScale carries its own `<summary>`. The population is Min, Max, Step and Default at ObjectScale.cs:5-8, read from the file.

Each of the two public methods on ObjectScale carries a `<summary>`, a `<param name="current">` and a `<returns>`. The population is StepUp at ObjectScale.cs:10 and StepDown at ObjectScale.cs:11, each taking one `float current`. The `<param>` requirement is not an embellishment: dotnet-format.md:370 requires documentation on "All public types, members, and parameters", and the worked example at dotnet-format.md:380-397 documents a parameter with a `<param>` tag.

ObjectKind receives a type-level `<summary>` only, and does NOT receive per-member summaries. Verified by counting `<summary>` tags in ObjectKind.cs before and after: the count rises by exactly 1, from 1 to 2. The type-level summary points the reader at the file's own grouping comments rather than restating them; those comments are at ObjectKind.cs:11, :18, :32, :42 and :49 (Doors, Furniture, Storage, Lighting, Decoration), read with `grep -n '^\s*//'`. The row MASTER-131 asks for member summaries on 37 members; the member count is in fact 38 by two independent predicates that agree (measurement.md section 3), and documenting 38 enum members individually is not what this XS-to-S row authorizes.
The existing `<summary>` on ObjectKind.None at ObjectKind.cs:5-8 is preserved verbatim, its `<see cref="PlacedObject"/>` included. Preservation criterion, deliberately satisfied at startRef.

Every documentation comment this task writes puts its tag description on a new line indented with `///` plus two tabs, and uses no single-line tag form. Verified two ways over the six owned files: `grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*/// {2,}'` returns 0 lines, and `grep -nE '///[[:space:]]*<(param|summary|returns)[^>]*>.*</(param|summary|returns)>'` returns 0 lines. This encodes dotnet-format.md:375, section 9: "Tag descriptions go on a **new line**, indented with **two tabs** from the `///` marker". Both predicates were validated by the architect before being written here: the first returns exactly the 4 known space-indented lines in CanvasPoint.cs and PlacedObjectDto.cs and returns 0 for the conforming control GetDungeonsQueryHandler.cs; the second returns the 14 known single-line tags across the three T3 files and does not match a conforming multi-line opener such as PlacedObject.cs:43.

Every description is a complete sentence ending in a period, and no sentence is broken across two `///` lines. This encodes dotnet-format.md:378, section 9: "Line breaks occur only at sentence boundaries. Never break a sentence across multiple `///` lines. Each new `///` continuation line begins a new sentence." Checked by reading the comments this task wrote. It is called out explicitly because measurement.md section 3 records an existing unfiled violation of this same rule elsewhere in the repository, so the dominant local form cannot be relied on as the guide.

Preservation criterion, deliberately satisfied at startRef: the ObjectRotation members are still spelled CW90, CW180 and CW270. Verified by `grep -n 'CW90\|CW180\|CW270'` on ObjectRotation.cs returning the three member lines :6, :7 and :8. Renaming them is excluded by escalation E1 because ObjectRotation is persisted by member name through `HasConversion<string>()` at PlacedObjectConfiguration.cs:30-32, so a rename rewrites every stored value. This task documents those members; it must not rename them.

Every file this task touches still has CRLF line endings on every line, and `sed -i` was not used. Verified by `cat -A` on each modified file showing `^M$` on every line. Load-bearing per measurement.md section 4, and doubly so here because this task's edits are entirely whitespace-sensitive documentation.

The six owned files are the only files this task modified, and the renamed file is still at src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/RotationDirection.cs rather than having been recreated at the old path. Verified by `ls` on both the old and new paths.

The existing tests AreaOutlineChangeTrackingTests.LoadAsync_AfterAnOutlineEdit_ReturnsTheEditedOutline (assertion at src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/AreaOutlineChangeTrackingTests.cs:154) and the loaded-aggregate assertion at that file's :92 both still pass. These two are the guard for the one real hazard in this remedy: Area.Outline is a value-converted property mapped with `.HasField("_outline")` and `PropertyAccessMode.PreferFieldDuringConstruction` at AreaConfiguration.cs:97-98, so EF writes the field by reflection. Revert the injection before reporting done.

The comment at AreaConfiguration.cs:18-21 no longer asserts in the present tense that "Area.Outline returns _outline.AsReadOnly() -- a fresh wrapper on every read", because this task makes that sentence false. It is rewritten to record that the wrapper is now cached, to state that OutlineComparer is still required, and to say why. tasks.title: Rename ct to cancellationToken across Application and Infrastructure, and obj to a descriptive local
acceptance: `grep -rn 'CancellationToken ct\b' src/DungeonMaster.Application src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure --include=*.cs`, with /obj/ and /bin/ paths excluded, returns 0 lines. The baseline is 51 declaration sites, 44 in Application and 7 in Infrastructure, re-derived by the architect per project with that command and agreeing with measurement.md section 3. This encodes dotnet-format.md:36, section 1 Naming, whose Parameter row gives the example `cancellationToken`. The predicate was validated both ways in measurement.md section 3: a positive control, `grep -c 'CancellationToken ct\b'` on Common/Dispatch/IQueryHandler.cs, returns 1; a near-miss that must not match, `grep -c 'CancellationToken cancellationToken'` on the same file, returns 0.

AMENDED A1. `grep -rn 'param name="ct"' src/DungeonMaster.Application src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure --include=*.cs`, with /obj/ and /bin/ excluded, returns 0 lines. **The scope is these two projects, not all of `src`.** As originally frozen this criterion was src-wide, which made it unsatisfiable alongside criterion 6: the 15 remaining `<param name="ct">` tags all sit in src/DungeonMaster.Tests, and all 15 of those files also hold a live `CancellationToken ct` declaration inside criterion 6's preservation set, so the tags document parameters that still exist and are correct today. Renaming them would have pointed 15 tags at parameters that do not exist -- manufacturing exactly the stale-tag defect this criterion was written to catch. Amended under escalation E5 by user authorization; the 15 tags travel to the backlog with the 28 parameters they document, so one later pass renames both together. The baseline within the amended scope was 17 occurrences, and the src-wide baseline was 32 occurrences across 26 files, both re-derived by T5 with `grep -rn` and `grep -rln`. This criterion exists as its own line because THE BUILD CANNOT CATCH IT, established by experiment rather than belief: `GenerateDocumentationFile` is set nowhere in the repository (`grep -rn 'GenerateDocumentationFile' --include=*.props --include=*.csproj` returns no hits), and in a scratch net10.0 classlib carrying this repository's own TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, AnalysisLevel=10.0, AnalysisMode=Recommended and EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true from Directory.Build.props, a method with a `<param name="ct">` tag over a `cancellationToken` parameter built with 0 Warning(s) and 0 Error(s); the same file with GenerateDocumentationFile=true added failed with `error CS1572: XML comment has a param tag for 'ct', but there is no parameter by that name` and `error CS1573`. So a clean build is a proxy here and would pass an implementation that renamed all 51 parameters and left every doc tag stale.

Every `<paramref name="ct"/>` reference is renamed with its parameter. Verified by `grep -rn 'paramref name="ct"' src --include=*.cs` with /obj/ and /bin/ excluded returning 0 lines. Same reasoning as the criterion above: without the documentation file, the compiler never validates a paramref either.

`grep -nw 'obj' src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/FloorObjectMethods.cs` returns 0 lines. The baseline is 9 occurrences across three distinct locals, at :31, :38, :41, :56, :59, :64, :95, :98 and :103, re-derived by the architect with that command and agreeing with measurement.md section 3. Note that MASTER-130 cites the local at FloorObjectMethods.cs:40, where measurement.md establishes there is no `obj` at all. This encodes dotnet-format.md:42, section 1: "Use descriptive names in lambda expressions - never single-letter variables", and the Parameter and local naming rows of the table at dotnet-format.md:26-36.

At FloorObjectMethods.cs:56-57 and :95-96 the local and the lambda parameter end up with two DIFFERENT descriptive names. Both sites today read `var obj = _objects.FirstOrDefault(placedObject => placedObject.Id == objectId)`, so renaming the local to `placedObject` would give the local and the lambda parameter the same name. The architect verified by compiling a standalone net10.0 classlib mirroring that exact shape that this is NOT a compile error on this toolchain - it built with 0 Warning(s) and 0 Error(s), and the build's error path was proven live in the same scratch project by an injected CS0029 that produced 1 Error(s) - so the compiler will not force the issue and this must be checked by reading. It encodes dotnet-format.md:42's requirement that lambda names be descriptive, which a name reused from the enclosing local is not.

Preservation criterion, deliberately satisfied at startRef: `grep -rn 'CancellationToken ct\b' src/DungeonMaster.Tests src/DungeonMaster.App src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests src/DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests --include=*.cs`, with /obj/ and /bin/ excluded, still returns 28 lines - the 27 Tests sites and 1 App site measurement.md section 3 measured, which the architect re-derived per project. Escalation E2 fixed this task's scope at Application plus Infrastructure and routed those 28 to the backlog, so touching them puts the task outside its agreed scope. The rename cannot break those projects' build: `grep -rn '\bct:' src --include=*.cs` with /obj/ and /bin/ excluded returns 0, so no call site anywhere passes the parameter by name, and C# does not require an implementation's parameter names to match its interface's.

Verified by reading the diff of each interface in src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Dispatch and src/DungeonMaster.Application/Common/Interfaces and confirming only identifier spellings inside parameter lists changed.

acceptance: A new test file exists at src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/CollectionWrapperCachingTests.cs and is the only file this task creates or modifies. Added under escalation E7 by user authorization, because T4's criteria 1 to 5 each require the caching to be 'proven by a test' and no task in the frozen manifest owned a test file -- the proof existed only as an uncommitted scratch harness, which disappears with the scratch directory and leaves the caching with no regression guard.

Five assertions, one per site, each proving that two successive reads of the property on the same instance return REFERENCE-equal objects: Dungeon.Floors, Area.Outline, Floor.Areas, Floor.Objects and MapDrawingSession.Vertices. Use whichever of ReferenceEquals or Should().BeSameAs this suite already uses -- determine that by reading the suite, not by assuming it.

A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MUST FAIL is included and its result reported: assert that two successive AsReadOnly() calls on a plain backing List<T> are NOT reference-equal, which is the pre-change shape. Without it, five passing reference-equality assertions could pass against an implementation returning the same empty singleton, or against a test that never exercises the property at all, and the file would look like a guard while guarding nothing.

Each of the five assertions is shown able to fail, by injected defect: revert one site at a time to the `_backing.AsReadOnly()` property-body form, observe that site's assertion fail, report the observed failure output, and revert the injection before reporting done. A reference-equality assertion never seen red is not a guard.

Area.Outline's assertion additionally exercises the EF materialisation path rather than only an in-memory aggregate, because that is the one site where the constructor-cached form was measured to fail: EF assigns a new List<PathSegment> over the _outline field after construction. If exercising the EF path in this file is not feasible, say so explicitly and state what the in-memory assertion does and does not cover. Do not present an in-memory-only assertion as covering the materialisation case.
